title: Can a wrist tell washing from the other home tasks? A small-N recognition of ICF d510

dataset.name: HTAD: Home-Tasks Activities Dataset (wrist accelerometer + audio)
dataset.record: wrist accelerometer @ ~31 Hz, 3 subjects, seven home tasks including WASHING HANDS (ICF d510), brushing teeth, eating chips, sweeping, mopping, typing, watching TV
dataset.citation: Garcia-Ceja E, Thambawita V, Hicks SA, Jha D, Jakobsen P, Hammer HL, Halvorsen P, Riegler MA. HTAD: A Home-Tasks Activities Dataset with Wrist-accelerometer and Audio Features. MMM 2021, LNCS 12573:196-205. doi:10.1007/978-3-030-67835-7_17.

proposition: Washing (ICF d510, washing oneself) is the self-care task with no data in the HMP wrist dataset. HTAD is the one public wrist-accelerometer set that labels WASHING HANDS. Under leave-one-subject-out, the ecosystem's HAR pipeline recognises washing at 0.53 recall -- about 3.7x the 0.14 chance level -- across a seven-task home-activity problem, cross-subject. This is a small-N (3 subjects) demonstration that washing is recognisable from a real wrist accelerometer, honestly not a definitive validation.

claims.statement: washing recall in the per-class table (cross-check)

validation.reference: The dataset's own per-trial activity labels (ground truth), scored with a strict leave-one-subject-out protocol over all seven home tasks
validation.data: REAL -- HTAD wrist accelerometer (Garcia-Ceja et al. 2021), 3 subjects, ~31 Hz
validation.note: HONEST scope, prominently: N = 3 subjects. Leave-one-subject-out means training on 2 people and testing on the third, so the estimate is noisy -- this is a DEMONSTRATION that washing hands carries a wrist-detectable signature above chance (0.53 vs 0.14, ~3.7x), not a definitive validation. Washing is confusable with the other hand-based tasks (brushing, eating). ICF d510 also covers bathing/showering, which HTAD does not contain; only hand-washing is tested. The coverage registry records this as `HTAD N=3, recall 0.53` so the weak evidence is visible wherever d510 appears.

open_questions.q: Three subjects is too few for a definitive washing (d510) validation; a larger labelled wrist-IMU set with bathing/hand-washing would confirm it, and no public wrist dataset yet labels dressing (d540) or toileting (d530). Documented, not escalated.
